The instructional setting is not merely repeated wording: in Grade R the statement sits under Term 3 'EMERGENT READING' / 'Emergent reading skills' in a purely pre-reading programme, whereas in Grade 1 Term 1 it sits under 'READING AND PHONICS' / 'Emergent reading skills (taught in Shared and Group Guided Reading lessons)' alongside daily phonemic-awareness and phonics instruction, i.e. the same listening-and-discussion capability applied to longer and more varied texts within formal shared/group guided reading. Grade R proficiency in attending to and talking about texts read aloud plausibly supports success with the Grade 1 version, so buildsTowards from the Grade R statement to the Grade 1 statement is supported; relatesTo would understate the clear cross-grade ordering. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both endpoints and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the bounded excerpts may not show all printed qualifiers.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0) Skills: the first is Term 4 EMERGENT WRITING / 'Emergent Writing:' — "'Writes' and asks others to give meaning to what has been written" — and the second is Term 3 EMERGENT READING / 'Emergent reading skills' — "Distinguishes pictures from print: points to a word and asks what the word is". judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 1 (resolved coordinate, rank 1), Term 2, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', printed as distinct bullets in the same table row on page 68 but under different Sub-strands: 'Group Guided Reading' for 'Continues to build a sight vocabulary from the incidental reading programme, the graded reading series and high-frequency word lists', and 'Paired/Independent Reading (twice a week in Language focus time)' for 'Reads to a partner from prepared or known texts to develop fluency'. Merge notes confirm these are separate printed statements rather than duplicates. They cohere substantively as complementary components of the same term's reading programme: growing automatic recognition of sight and high-frequency words (LC tags: sight vocabulary, high-frequency words, graded reading) and oral fluency practice with a partner (LC tags: fluency, paired reading, known texts) mutually reinforce reading development. However, the evidence does not support a developmental direction: both are co-timed outcomes of the same Grade and the same Term in separate sub-strands/contact-time slots, neither statement shows expanded scope, greater complexity, or increased independence relative to the other, and the fluency statement is explicitly bounded to 'prepared or known texts', which deliberately limits reliance on an expanding sight-word store. Nomination signals (shared ancestors, rank_gap 0, weak page proximity, low jaccard overlap on function words 'a', 'from', 'to') are structural only and cannot license buildsTowards. This is meaningful reinforcement without dependency, so the symmetric relatesTo is correct, with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Upstream audit/merge context and truncated source/LC evidence on both endpoints limit, but do not contradict, this reading.

Proficiency with copying letters/numerals and distinguishing writing from drawing plausibly supports success in copying environmental print in play. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0, resolved coordinates). The second SFI, 'Makes up own story by \'reading\' the pictures', is Term 1 / Emergent Reading / 'Emergent reading skills'; the first SFI, 'Orders a sequence of pictures and relates the story created', is Term 2 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning'. Term 1 to Term 2 is a permitted within-grade forward direction. The shared capability (interpreting pictures to generate an oral story, LC 'Interprets pictures to make up own story' and LC 'Relates the story created from the ordered pictures') is substantively extended in Term 2 by the added demand of physically ordering a picture sequence (LC 'Sequences pictures', tags sequencing/visual cues) and then narrating the resulting coherent story, i.e. narrative construction constrained by a learner-imposed sequence rather than free picture-reading. Competence in making up a story from pictures plausibly supports success with sequencing-plus-retelling, so a developmental direction from the earlier-term picture-reading skill to the later-term sequencing-and-relating skill is supported rather than mere repeated wording. Evidence limitation: both endpoints have truncated source evidence and the second endpoint has truncated LC evidence, so only the bounded excerpts were used.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 (rank 2) Skill statements under Reading and Phonics > 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' (Phonics). The second SFI sits in Term 1 ('Recognises rhyming words such as rack, sack, back, lack, pack', identity scope grade 2|term 1) and the first in Term 3 ('Recognises vowel digraphs and diphthongs such as oy, oi, ay, ai', identity scope grade 2|term 3), so the only permitted within-grade developmental direction is earlier Term 1 to later Term 3. The change is substantive rather than repeated wording: Term 1 rhyme recognition works with whole shared rimes (-ack) and sound patterns (LC tags: phonics, rhyming words, sounds), whereas Term 3 requires recognising specific multi-letter vowel grapheme units — digraphs and diphthongs (LC tags: vowel digraphs, diphthongs, phonics). Facility in hearing and matching shared vowel-plus-ending patterns in rhyming word families plausibly supports success in isolating and recognising vowel digraph/diphthong spellings, consistent with the Term 1 table context that introduces common vowel digraphs and the Term 3 context that extends blends/digraphs work. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), and the nomination's lexical overlap ('recognises', 'such as') alone was not treated as progression evidence.
